summary.one_liner: Git Town is a command-line tool that adds Git commands for automating the creation, syncing, shipping, and cleanup of branches.
summary.what_it_does: Git Town provides extra Git subcommands for branch workflows. Its basic commands create an up-to-date feature branch (hack), sync existing branches and remove shipped ones (sync), switch branches through a text UI (switch), and open a pull or merge request (propose). For stacked changes it offers commands to append, prepend, combine, detach, swap, and reparent branches, plus diff-parent to show a branch's committed changes. It also has commands to limit syncing (contribute, observe, park, prototype), recovery commands for interrupted runs (continue, skip, status, undo, runlog), setup and configuration commands (config, init, offline, completions), and advanced commands (branch hierarchy view, compress, delete, rename, repo, ship). The README says it works with Git Flow, GitHub Flow, GitLab Flow, and trunk-based development, and supports mono-repos.
use_cases: Create a new feature branch from up-to-date main
Keep many local branches in sync with their parents
Clean up branches already merged and shipped
Open pull or merge requests from the command line
Recover from Git merge conflicts during automated branch operations
how_to_run: See the installation and configuration instructions on the Git Town website (link referenced in README; commands not given in README)
Run `git town help [command]` to show help for a command
notable: Supports Git Flow, GitHub Flow, GitLab Flow, and trunk-based development
Stacked-change commands such as append, prepend, swap, and combine
Undo and runlog commands to inspect or reverse recent Git Town operations
Shell completions for bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell
Offline mode and per-branch syncing controls (park, observe, contribute)
caveats: README does not include install commands; it points to the external website for installation and configuration
